answer: The morning train was crowded, but I found a seat near the door. I left my umbrella on the rack and remembered it before the next stop. A woman across the aisle pointed it out when I stood up. I thanked her and walked to the office from the station. The rain had stopped by then, and the pavement was still wet. I arrived before the meeting and had time to make tea. Nobody else was in the room yet.

We checked the garden after breakfast and found three tomatoes ready to pick. The smaller plant still has green fruit, so we left it alone. I watered the herbs beside the steps and moved the empty pots into the shed. The hose was leaking near the tap, and I put a bucket under it. We can look for a replacement washer this weekend if the shop is open. The fence also needs paint, but that can wait until the weather is dry.

At the workshop, Maya showed me how to adjust the little wooden clamp. I tried it on a scrap piece before touching the shelf. The first joint was loose, so I measured the width again and cut another piece. That one fit without forcing it. We swept the floor together and put the tools back in their marked places. I took the remaining boards home because I want to finish the shelf there. Maya kept the drawing for the next class.

The library called this afternoon to say that the book I requested has arrived. I cannot collect it today because I am waiting for a delivery. Tomorrow I will take the bus there after lunch, provided the parcel arrives in the morning. I also need to return the two books on my desk. One belongs to my sister, so I will give it to her instead of leaving it at the library. The other book is due on Friday.

I made soup for dinner with the carrots and beans left in the fridge. The recipe called for lemon, but we had none, so I used a little vinegar. I kept the salt low because Dad prefers to add his own. There is enough for two lunches tomorrow, and the containers are on the top shelf. Please let the soup cool before putting the lids on. The bread is in the freezer if anyone wants some with it.

Our group met by the river just after sunrise and followed the path toward the old bridge. The path was muddy in places, so we walked slowly and stayed together. We saw a small boat tied to the bank, but nobody was aboard. After the bridge we stopped for water and checked the map. The shorter route back was closed, so we returned the same way. I reached the car before the rain began and waited there for the others.

The parcel arrived with a torn corner, but the bowl inside was intact. I photographed the box before opening the rest of the wrapping. The note said the second bowl would come separately, and there was no date for that delivery. I put the first bowl on the kitchen shelf and saved the packing paper. If the second package has not arrived by Monday, I will contact the shop. For now there is nothing else we need to do.

During the rehearsal, the lights went out for a few minutes. We stayed on stage while the technician checked the switch near the entrance. Someone opened the curtains so we could see the floor. When the lights came back, we started the scene from the beginning. The music was too quiet at first, and the technician raised it after we stopped. We finished the rehearsal on time and agreed to meet half an hour earlier on Saturday.

I sorted the photographs into two boxes this evening. The blue box holds pictures from family trips, and the red box holds pictures from school. I found one photograph without a date and left it on the table for Mum to see. There were also several empty envelopes in the drawer, which I recycled. I did not throw away any photographs. Tomorrow I want to label the boxes and put them on the shelf above the desk.

The plumber inspected the tap and said the handle needs a new part. She tightened the connection under the sink, which stopped the small drip for now. She will call when the part arrives, but she did not promise a date. I moved the cleaning supplies out of the cupboard so she could reach the pipe. They are still in the hallway, and I will put them back after the floor is dry. The kitchen sink can be used in the meantime.

For the class project, we counted the birds from the bench for twenty minutes. We saw four crows near the gate and two pigeons on the roof. A small bird landed in the tree, but we could not identify it, so we recorded it as unknown. We did not count the birds we heard but could not see. Afterward we compared our notes and found that everyone had recorded the same six identified birds. The unknown bird stayed on our separate list.

I spoke with Arun about the trip after work. He can drive on Friday, but he is not sure whether he can return on Sunday. I said I would check the train times before we decide. We have already booked a room for two nights, and the booking can be changed until Wednesday. The museum closes early on Saturday, so we hope to visit in the morning. Nothing has been arranged for dinner, and we can decide that when we arrive.
